h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר מ״ח Pesach — Maamar Mem Ches
He Hurled Them to the Heights: Pharaoh's Six Hundred Chariots and the Apex of Impurity

p: סוּס וְרֹכְבוֹ רָמָה בַיָּם.
"Horse and its rider He hurled (ramah) into the sea"
(שְׁמוֹת ט"ו, א').
(Shemos 15:1).
בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
In the Midrash
(תַּנְחוּמָא בְּשַׁלַּח י"ג):
(Tanchuma Beshalach 13):
כְּתִיב "רָמָה בַיָּם" וּכְתִיב "יָרָה בַיָּם" — כֵּיצַד יִתְקַיְּימוּ שְׁנֵי מִקְרָאוֹת אֵלּוּ? "רָמָה" — שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹלִים לַמָּרוֹם, "יָרָה" — שֶׁהָיוּ יוֹרְדִין לַתְּהוֹם.

"It is written 'He hurled (ramah) into the sea' [v. 1] and it is written 'He cast (yarah) into the sea' [v. 4]—how are these two verses reconciled? Ramah [from ram, high] means they were thrown upward to the heights, and yarah means they were plunged downward to the depths."
"לַמָּרוֹם" נִרְאֶה שֶׁפֵּירוּשׁוֹ לַשָּׁמַיִם, וְאֵין לוֹ פֵּירוּשׁ—וּבְפֵירוּשׁ רַשִׁ"י הַגִּירְסָא "לָרוּם", אַךְ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ וּמְכִילְתָּא וְיַלְקוּט וּפְסִיקְתָּא הַגִּירְסָא "לַמָּרוֹם".

"To the heights (la'marom)" appears to mean toward the heavens, which seems inexplicable—and in Rashi's commentary the reading is la'rum ("upward"), yet in the Midrash, Mechilta, Yalkut, and Pesikta the reading is la'marom.
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן: דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
However, the explanation lies in what is stated in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' מ"ו.):
שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת — אַמַּאי? לָקֳבֵל מִנְיָינָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, דִּכְתִיב: שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת אֶלֶף רַגְלִי וְכוּלֵּי.
"'Six hundred [chosen chariots]'—why six hundred? Corresponding to the count of Israel, as it is written, 'Six hundred thousand footmen, etc.'"
וְאַף דִּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל "אֶלֶף", וְכָאן יְחִידִים
Now even though regarding Israel it is six hundred thousand whereas here it is mere single units [six hundred chariots]
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
the explanation follows what is brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק א' קס"א.):
וּבִרְכָתָא לָאו אִיהוּ פָּחוֹת מֵאֶלֶף וְכוּלֵּי
"And blessing is never less than a thousand, etc."
וְהָעִנְיָן דִּבְעוֹלָם הָאֲצִילוּת הַמִּסְפָּר אֶחָד, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֵפֶר יְצִירָה
for in the World of Emanation (Atzilus) the number is one, as they said in Sefer Yetzirah
(Chapter 1):
וְלִפְנֵי אֶחָד מָה אַתָּה סוֹפֵר?
"And before One, what do you count?"
וּבַבְּרִיאָה מִסְתָּעֵף עַד עֶשֶׂר, וּבַיְּצִירָה שֶׁכָּלוּל גַּם כֵּן מֵעֶשֶׂר הַמִּסְפָּר מֵאָה, וּכְשֶׁבָּא הַבְּרָכָה לְעוֹלָם הָעֲשִׂיָּה שֶׁכָּלוּל מֵעֶשֶׂר הַמִּסְפָּר הוּא אֶלֶף;

and in the World of Creation (Beriah) it expands to ten, in the World of Formation (Yetzirah)—which also comprises ten—the number is one hundred, and when blessing descends into the World of Action (Asiyah)—comprising another ten—the number is one thousand;
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמַּ"ע מִפָּאנוֹ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה שֶׁמִּסְפָּר הָאַחֲרוֹן אֶלֶף וְרִבּוֹא הוּא רַק רִיבּוּי, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נֶחְשָׁב גַּם כֵּן מִיחִידִיּוֹת.
and thus the Rama of Fano, of blessed memory, wrote that the final numerical orders of thousand and myriad are merely multipliers, after which counting resumes from single units.
וְעִנְיַן שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת: שְׁנֵי שִׁינִּי"ן
And the meaning of "six hundred" is two Shins [each Shin = 300]
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
based on what is brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' ר"ד.):
ש' רָזָא דִּתְלַת אֲבָהָן,
"Shin is the secret of the three Patriarchs,"
וּבְמָקוֹם אַחֵר
and in another place
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג' רנ"ז.):
(Ra'aya Mehemna, Zohar, Vol. 3, 257a):
שְׁכִינְתָּא אִתְקְרִיאַת מִסִּטְרָא דִּתְלַת דַּרְגִּין עִילָּאִין דְּאִינּוּן ש', תְּלַת כִּתְרִין: כֶּתֶר, חָכְמָה, בִּינָה וְכוּלֵּי
"The Shechinah is called [Shabbos] from the aspect of the three supernal levels which are Shin, the three crowns: Kesser, Chochmah, Binah, etc."
וְהַכֹּל אֶחָד, שֶׁהֵם עֲנָפִים מִשָּׁלֹשׁ רִאשׁוֹנוֹת
and both are one, for the Patriarchs are branches of the first three Sefiros
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' קע"ה.),
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 175b),
וּמֵאָה מִסְפָּר שָׁלֵם
while one hundred is a complete number
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק א' קכ"ג.),
(Zohar, Vol. 1, 123a),
וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל הָיָה שֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת אֶלֶף, שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל נִתְבָּרְרוּ מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ רֵאשִׁית הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה עַד עוֹלָם הָעֲשִׂיָּה, דְּשָׁם הַמִּסְפָּר אֶלֶף.
so Israel numbered six hundred thousand, because Israel were refined from the root of primordial thought all the way down to the World of Action, where the number is one thousand.
וְהַמִּצְרִים רָצוּ לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יְדֵי רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה שֶׁהוּא אֶחָד זֶה לְעוּמַּת זֶה, וְזֶה שֶׁמּוּבָא אַחַר כָּךְ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
Now the Egyptians sought to overpower them through the apex of impurity, which is "One" on the unholy side corresponding to holiness, and this is what is brought afterward in the holy Zohar
וְשָׁלִשִׁים עַל כֻּלּוֹ — כּוּלָּא בְּחָכְמְתָא, לָקֳבֵל דַּרְגִּין עִילָּאִין, תְּרֵין וְחַד
"'And officers (shalishim, lit. "thirds/three") over all of it (kulo)'—all through [sorcerous] wisdom, corresponding to the supernal levels, two and one"
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁהִתְגַּבֵּר כָּל כָּךְ בַּקְּלִיפָּה:
meaning Pharaoh empowered himself to such an extreme in the realm of impurity:
וּכְמוֹ דִּבְקְדוּשָּׁה כְּתִיב
for just as in holiness it is written
(Mishlei 2:10):
כִּי תָבוֹא חָכְמָה בְלִבֶּךָ וְדַעַת לְנַפְשְׁךָ יִנְעָם
"For wisdom shall enter your heart, and knowledge shall be pleasant to your soul"
חָכְמָה מוֹחָא, בִּינָה לִיבָּא, שֶׁבְּחִיבּוּר חָכְמָה וּבִינָה, מוֹחָא וְלִיבָּא, יוֹלִיד הַדַּעַת שֶׁהוּא פְּנִימִיּוּת מִכֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן,
Chochmah being the brain and Binah the heart, so that through the union of Chochmah and Binah (brain and heart) is born Da'as, the inwardness of Kesser Elyon

כֵּן בַּקְּלִיפָּה בְּזֶה לְעוּמַּת זֶה יֵשׁ חָכְמַת מִצְרַיִם, מוֹחָא, וּבִינָה — נָחָשׁ אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים, לֵב כְּסִיל לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ, חֵשֶׁק לְתַאֲווֹת רָעוֹת, וְהִתְגַּבֵּר תְּרֵין וְחַד עַל כּוּלּוֹ, רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה

so too in impurity, one corresponding to the other, there is the "wisdom of Egypt" (unholy brain) and unholy Binah—the Serpent, the "wife of harlotry," the fool's heart at his left, craving evil lusts—and Pharaoh empowered himself with "two and one" over "all of it," the apex of impurity
לֹא הַדַּעַת, שֶׁדַּעַת דִּקְלִיפָּה הוּא בִּלְעָם, וְהָיָה בַּקְּלִיפָּה נֶגֶד מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
not unholy Da'as, for the Da'as of impurity was Bilam, who stood in impurity opposite Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, as they said
(בְּמִדְבַּר רַבָּה י"ד, י"ט):
(Bamidbar Rabbah 14:19):
וְלֹא קָם עוֹד נָבִיא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמֹשֶׁה, אֲבָל בְּאוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם קָם, וּמַנּוּ? בִּלְעָם
"'And there arose no prophet again in Israel like Moshe,' but among the nations of the world there did arise one, and who was he? Bilam"
שֶׁהָיָה בַּקְּלִיפָּה כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם, וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
who was in impurity the counterpart of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, as it is said
(בְּמִדְבַּר כ"ד, ט"ז):
(Bamidbar 24:16):
יֹדֵעַ דַּעַת עֶלְיוֹן
"Who knows the knowledge (Da'as) of the Most High"
דַּעַת דִּקְלִיפָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר
unholy Da'as, as brought in the Zohar
(חֵלֶק ג' קצ"ד.);
אֲבָל רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה הוּא עֲמָלֵק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
whereas the apex (Reishis) of impurity is Amalek, as it is said
(בְּמִדְבַּר כ"ד, כ'):
(Bamidbar 24:20):
רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק,
"The first (reishis) of nations is Amalek,"

וּכְמוֹ דִּבְקְדוּשָּׁה כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן אִיהוּ כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת, כֵּן בַּקְּלִיפָּה רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה אִיהוּ מַלְכוּת דִּקְלִיפָּה, וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי אֱדוֹם נִקְרָא בַּשַּׁ"ס מַלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה, מַלְכוּת חַיָּיבָא;

and just as in holiness Kesser Elyon is Kesser Malchus, so in impurity the apex of impurity is the Malchus of impurity, which is why Edom is called in the Talmud "the wicked kingdom" (Malchus ha'resha'ah / Malchus chayava);
וּפַרְעֹה נִתְגַּבֵּר בַּקְּלִיפּוֹת: וְשָׁלִשִׁים עַל כֻּלּוֹ—תְּרֵין: חָכְמָה וּבִינָה דִּקְלִיפָּה, וְחַד: רֵאשִׁית דִּקְלִיפָּה, וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר "עַל כֻּלּוֹ".
thus Pharaoh empowered himself in the husks—"and officers (shalishim) over all of it"—two (unholy Chochmah and Binah) and one (the apex of impurity, which is meant by "over all of it").
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: "רָמָה בַיָּם" — שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹלִין לַמָּרוֹם, וְהַיְינוּ מָרוֹם דִּקְלִיפָּה; "יָרָה" — שֶׁהָיוּ יוֹרְדִין לַתְּהוֹם, וְאֵין נִפְרָדִין זֶה מִזֶּה.

And this is what the Midrash meant by "Ramah into the sea—that they rose up to the heights (marom)," meaning the arrogant heights of impurity, and "Yarah—that they plunged down to the depths," for the two are inseparable from one another.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Sukkos 24 — “Samael includes all ten attributes of impurity. And the ayah [bird], as is brought from the holy Arizal, alludes to the first three: Alef, Pele Elyon, is Kesser Elyon; Yud-Hei are Chochmah and Binah. So too in impurity there is an ayah that includes the first three of impurity, such as Bilam, who was the da’as of impurity, as is written in the Zohar, and da’as includes all the first three; so too in impurity. And Amalek, ‘the first of nations,’ is the reishis of impurity, and Amalek and Bilam are one, for their deeds intermingle.” Connection: The same mapping of the upper levels of impurity, Bilam as its da’as and Amalek as its reishis; it adds that the two are a single root, and applies it to the sukkah that shields from Bilam’s gaze.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Shevi'i shel Pesach 33 — “Hashem arranged in holiness that perfection is ‘two and one,’ for thereby room is given for man to recognize His unity: only because Hashem set an attribute and its opposite, right and left, can a person recognize that there is One above them both. Israel follow this recognition and do not sink into any one attribute, but follow His unity and simple will. Opposite this Pharaoh made ‘officers over all of it,’ two and one like the pattern above, boasting that he too held of the two and one and received all his strength from the simple will, which set even darkness in the world. And ‘his chosen officers were drowned in the Sea of Reeds.’” Connection: Both read the Zohar’s ‘two and one’ as Pharaoh’s counterfeit of the upper structure; Sod Yesharim explains the ‘one’ as the simple will above both sides, which Pharaoh claimed as his source.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Yehudah Aryeh Leib Alter, Sefas Emes, Pesach 5645 — “In Egypt was the root of all idolatry in the world.  The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to uproot the entire root, and therefore their heavenly prince also came down, so that he too would have a downfall. ‘For He is exalted over the exalted’: not like flesh and blood, who brings his fellow down from his greatness; rather the Holy One, blessed be He, raised them up to all the root and all the exaltation they could possibly have, and afterward cast them down. This is ‘horse and its rider’: the Egyptians below together with their root above; and this is ‘ramah into the sea, yarah into the sea,’ as Chazal said that they rose and went down.” Connection: The Sefas Emes reads the same Midrash as the raising of Egypt to the root of its power before its fall; Rav Tzadok names that root as the apex of impurity.
